papers.title: Mindfulness-Based Interventions for Tinnitus Distress: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, and Appraisal of Intervention Reporting.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: The aims of this study were to evaluate the effects of mindfulness-based interventions on tinnitus-related distress and to appraise the reporting of intervention content in the tinnitus literature. METHOD: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted. Eight electronic databases were searched on August 12, 2025, with an updated search on April 2, 2026. Studies of adults with chronic bothersome tinnitus receiving mindfulness-based interventions were eligible. Seventeen reports met the inclusion criteria for the systematic review. Quantitative synthesis was narrowed to one prioritized tinnitus-related outcome per study stream. The primary meta-analysis was restricted to controlled comparative studies, and a secondary exploratory meta-analysis examined within-arm pre-post change. RESULTS: Most controlled studies reported favorable findings for mindfulness-based interventions on tinnitus-related distress, whereas uncontrolled studies generally showed pre-post improvement signals. In the primary controlled comparative synthesis, six study streams contributed one prioritized outcome per study, yielding a pooled effect favoring mindfulness-based interventions: Hedges'  CONCLUSIONS: Mindfulness-based interventions were associated with reduced tinnitus-related distress, and controlled comparative evidence was positive but still imprecise. Stronger comparative trials and more rigorous reporting of intervention implementation and fidelity are needed to support clinical translation.
